Record Class PanelTreeLayout

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.trevlar.menukit.core.PanelTreeLayout
Record Components:
bounds - layout-local bounds per panel ID (from PanelLayout.resolve)
layoutOriginX - leftmost x across visible panels (0 if none visible)
layoutOriginY - topmost y across visible panels (0 if none visible)
totalWidth - horizontal extent across visible panels, clamped to minImageWidth
totalHeight - vertical extent across visible panels, clamped to minImageHeight
public record PanelTreeLayout(Map<String, PanelBounds> bounds, int layoutOriginX, int layoutOriginY, int totalWidth, int totalHeight) extends Record
Phase 16j R1 — shared layout primitive across the standalone-screen (MK) and container-screen (MKC) rendering contexts. Bundles three operations that both contexts previously implemented in parallel:
  1. Per-panel size computation via a context-supplied panelSizeFn (MK derives size from elements + padding; MKC also factors in slot groups + pinned dims).
  2. Position resolution via PanelLayout.resolve(List, Map, int, int, int) (already context-neutral; this primitive just orchestrates the call).
  3. Layout-extent + origin derivation across visible panels, used by the consumer to drive screen-space centering (leftPos / topPos in MK; recenter() correction in MKC).

Hidden panels are excluded from extent calculation — toggling a panel hidden mid-frame collapses the layout naturally. When every panel is hidden, the result falls back to minImageWidth / minImageHeight centered at the origin so the centering math doesn't underflow.

Why a record instead of out-parameters

Java has no native multi-return; the alternatives were (a) passing mutable arrays/objects to fill, or (b) returning a small record. The record keeps the call site readable and the contract immutable.

What stays per-context

The centering math itself (translating layout-local origin into screen-space leftPos/topPos) lives in each context — MK applies it directly in computeLayout; MKC applies it post-super.init in recenter to override vanilla's centering. Both formulas are the same shape: leftPos = (screenW - totalWidth)/2 - originX.

  • Method Details

    • resolve

      public static PanelTreeLayout resolve(List<Panel> panels, Function<Panel,int[]> panelSizeFn, int bodyGap, int relativeGap, int titleHeight, int minImageWidth, int minImageHeight)
      Computes the layout for panels using panelSizeFn to derive each panel's pixel size. Sizes are computed for ALL panels (even hidden ones — they may become visible mid-frame and need stable layout-local coords); extent is calculated only across VISIBLE panels so toggled-hidden panels don't inflate the screen.
      Parameters:
      panels - panel tree to lay out (order matters — BODY panels stack in declaration order)
      panelSizeFn - per-context function mapping Panel → {width, height}
      bodyGap - vertical gap between BODY-stack siblings
      relativeGap - gap between an anchored panel and its anchor
      titleHeight - vertical space reserved above the first BODY panel
      minImageWidth - minimum image width (used in the degenerate all-hidden case AND as a clamp on the returned totalWidth)
      minImageHeight - same, vertical axis
